text: The Patriots head into Buffalo for an early AFC East showdown against the undefeated Bills sitting at 1-2, fresh off signing offensive lineman Matt Pryor from Arizona's practice squad—a move that comes after the team placed guard Greg Van Roten on injured reserve with a thigh injury, further depleting the infrastructure around quarterback Drake Maye. The rookie quarterback insists his right shoulder is fine and that he's capable of executing the offense, pinpointing instead a need for better decision-making to address the Patriots' anemic offensive output, which sits dead last in the NFL at 9.7 points per game. Meanwhile, analysts are questioning whether New England is deploying Maye optimally, while Josh Allen and the Bills will look to capitalize on a turnover-prone Patriots offense at their newly renovated Highmark Stadium—though Allen himself will be working to clean up the sloppy moments that have occasionally dotted Buffalo's 3-0 start. Off the field, Ann Maye, the quarterback's wife, volunteered at a local food pantry this week and helped present a $100,000 donation from the MayeDay Family Foundation to support families facing food insecurity.
